originality.rationale: The inspected primary source assumes a globally nondecreasing unbounded change bound. The claim isolates a different sufficient family: the bound need only be nondecreasing and unbounded along one computable positive-density reservoir, with one allowed change off it. published-finding corpus and accessible own-ledger searches found no same-statement result. This is an explicit structural extension by decomposition, not a claim to classify all nonmonotone bounds; an unindexed equivalent observation remains a risk.
residual_risks: The result is derived from established theorems; a direct corollary or equivalent coding argument may exist in unindexed literature.
The sufficient condition is not necessary, and bounds whose high-change threshold sets have irregular or vanishing density remain unclassified.
No independent audit has been performed.

value.rationale: The theorem isolates a meaningful resource principle: a computable positive-density reservoir can carry all unbounded mind-change capacity while the complement needs only one allowed change per coordinate. The explicit alternating bound demonstrates that global monotonicity and density-one high-change capacity are unnecessary for the full density spectrum. This is a useful sufficient condition for studying irregular bounds, while the scope is deliberately limited to avoid implying a full classification.
